uncited: This family defines methods for generating sequences of camera poses (position and orientation) for volume rendering, novel view synthesis, and 3D reconstruction.
It solves the problem of determining valid viewing geometries when real-world capture data is unavailable, insufficient, or requires optimization for specific computational constraints.

What sets this family apart from sibling methods like [Sky Gradient](1262-sky-gradient.md) or [Arcball Camera](1639-arcball-camera.md) is the focus on generating *temporal sequences* or *structured multi-view sets* rather than interactive single-view controls or static background models.

It differs from [Camera Ray Generation](7456-camera-ray-generation.md) by operating at the pose level (defining the camera's world transform) rather than the ray level (defining individual pixel rays), although it feeds directly into ray generation.

Camera trajectory generation is fundamental to novel view synthesis (NVS) and 3D reconstruction, where the goal is to render views from angles not captured during data acquisition.
